claims.text: The initial material is bulk as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported yield strength of 786 MPa.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported terminal strain of 13.5%.
The proposed treatment uses approximately 50% cold-rolling reduction.
The proposed treatment anneals the rolled alloy at approximately 800 °C for one hour.
Cold rolling followed by annealing will produce a refined, bimodal grain-size distribution with improved grain-boundary configurations.
Subsequent annealing promotes recrystallization and grain refinement.
The resulting microstructure enhances dislocation mobility.
The resulting microstructure promotes more uniform tensile plastic deformation.
The treatment will improve tensile uniform elongation by at least 20% relative to the stated 13.5% baseline.
The treated alloy will retain yield strength within ±10% of 786 MPa.
The treated alloy will retain compressive strength within ±10% of 1314 MPa.
The treatment will not reduce impact-triggered energy release by more than 10% relative to the as-cast control.
The tensile prediction applies at room temperature and a strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The hypothesis applies corresponding strain-rate limits of approximately 10^-3 s^-1 to compression and impact testing.
Existing studies have demonstrated impact-triggered energy release in HfZrTiTa0.53.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is identified as terminal strain in the initial-state and baseline fields but is treated as the baseline for tensile uniform elongation in the hypothesis and predicted outcome. Terminal strain and uniform elongation are not established as the same measurement.

The conditions call for impact tests under loading and rate conditions comparable to quasi-static tests at about 10^-3 s^-1, while also requiring impact-triggered energy release. The intended impact loading rate is therefore internally unclear.
